title: Strata Therapeutics - On-prem air-gapped discovery
summary: Intro discovery for on-prem, air-gapped deployment needs. Main concerns: offline updates, hardware footprint, KMS/HSM integration, SOC2/ISO, network segmentation. Discussed Dedicated vs Private/on-prem tradeoffs and pilot approach with benchmarks.
next_steps: Jordan to send on-prem deployment checklist and security whitepaper (incl. SOC2 docs)
Priya to share recommended machine/GPUs + sizing spreadsheet for 8k token LLMs
Customer to provide timeline constraints and procurement window by 2026-08-28
action_items: Jordan Lee: Share pricing for Dedicated vs Private options - due 2026-08-24
Priya Nair: Upload GPU sizing and sample benchmark numbers - due 2026-08-25
Lina Park: Send current encryption/KMS architecture diagram - due 2026-08-24
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-20 15:00 PDT | Duration: 48 minutes | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marco Alvarez (Redwood Solutions); Dr. Maya Santos (CTO), Ken Ito (Head of DevOps), Lina Park (Security Manager), Omar Ruiz (ML Engineer)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood, with Priya our SE. How are you all?
[00:07] Dr. Maya Santos: Hi Jordan, thanks. Doing well. I'll hand it over to the team - we booked this to understand Redwood's on-prem and air-gapped options.
[00:15] Jordan Lee: Absolutely. Quick agenda — understand your constraints, security needs, hardware footprint, and talk pilot scope. Priya, want to intro the product?
[00:22] Priya Nair: Sure. So Redwood provides three serving modes — hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private which is the on-prem / VPC install. For air-gapped we typically deploy the Private control plane with an offline bundle and the inference runtime inside your network. There are some trade-offs we should cover.
[00:40] Ken Ito: Quick note, we're regulated — pharma — so offline updates and no egress from our subnets is required. We can't have any outbound calls during inference.
[00:48] Priya Nair: Totally understood. We have customers in similar regulated spaces. For true air-gap, we do an offline transfer model: we produce an offline artifact (container images, model weights) signed and you import them via removable media into your internal registry.
[01:05] Lina Park: How do you handle key management for that? We use HSM-backed keys and our KMS.
[01:11] Marco Alvarez: Good question. We support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations. For air-gapped installs, the private control plane can be configured to use your on-prem HSM via PKCS#11 or an intermediary KMS adapter. There's some manual setup for certs and key material transfer.
[01:28] Omar Ruiz: When you say "support", does that mean Redwood communicates with our KMS, or the runtime uses local keys only?
[01:34] Priya Nair: The runtime can be configured to use local keys exclusively. For telemetry/call-home we can disable all outbound endpoints. The control plane (if you run it) can be isolated. The only time we touch keys is during packaging/signing which happens off network before you import.
[01:51] Ken Ito: Okay, and what about updates? Our security team will want to vet updates. We can't just auto-pull.
[01:57] Jordan Lee: Right — our update workflow for air-gapped customers is: we prepare a signed bundle, you run it in a staging environment, run your security scans, then promote to prod. We can also provide checksums and reproducible images.
[02:12] Dr. Maya Santos: Sounds good. What's the typical size of these bundles and frequency? Models are big, we've been working with 70-100GB weights for some variants.
[02:20] Priya Nair: Bundle size depends on model and quantization. For a 70GB FP16 model, an int8 quantized variant can be ~20-30GB. We recommend shipping quantized variants for on-prem to reduce transfer and footprint. Frequency: usually monthly for patches, but major model updates on your cadence.
[02:38] Ken Ito: Do you provide on-site assist for initial import? We have a tight procurement window and limited SRE time.
[02:44] Jordan Lee: We have professional services for on-site or remote install. For air-gapped installs that's common. We can scope a 3-5 day install + validation engagement.
[02:53] Lina Park: Our main concern: how do you ensure no telemetry leaks?
[02:58] Priya Nair: We can disable telemetry entirely and ship with an option file that turns off any outbound metrics. Logs can be written to local storage only. We also support local-only tracing sinks.
[03:09] Omar Ruiz: Performance question — we need to serve requests with +/- 100ms latency at 2-3 concurrent sessions for an 8k token LLM. Is that realistic on-prem?
[03:17] Priya Nair: Latency depends a lot on GPU type and KV-cache handling. For 8k contexts, on a single A100 or H100 class server with optimized kernels and batching disabled for low latency, sub-100ms is possible for smaller models but for larger dense models might be closer to 150-250ms per token. We should benchmark with your specific model.
[03:36] Ken Ito: We prefer NVIDIA H100s but procurement might push us to A100s or even lower-tier GPUs for cost reasons. What trade-offs do we expect?
[03:44] Marco Alvarez: H100 gives better throughput and faster mixed-precision ops; A100 is fine for many loads but you may see higher latency and lower max concurrency. We also provide quantization and kernel choices; those can reduce memory and improve latency on lower GPUs but sometimes at quality tradeoffs.
[04:02] Dr. Maya Santos: About quality — we cannot degrade outputs for certain tasks. Is there a way to run canary model comparisons?
[04:09] Priya Nair: Yes. Our rollouts support canary and A/B testing. For Private installs, you can run two model variants side-by-side and collect evaluation metrics locally. Redwood Optimize can help with automated regression alerts, but in air-gapped setups you might keep the eval harness in your environment.
[04:26] Lina Park: Compliance: do you have SOC2 / ISO docs we can provide to our auditors?
[04:31] Jordan Lee: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 artifacts. For on-prem, auditors usually want to see the same documentation plus the deployment runbook. We'll send you the whitepaper and the compliance pack.
[04:44] Ken Ito: Awesome. Procurement will want to see an estimated TCO vs using Redwood Hosted or Dedicated. Can you give a rough delta?
[04:52] Jordan Lee: High-level: Hosted is lowest operational friction but highest unit cost; Dedicated is a middle ground with reserved capacity and some isolation; Private/on-prem is highest up-front cost and ops, but gives control and may be cheaper at scale depending on GPU amortization. We'll include a TCO worksheet tailored to your projected qps.
[05:10] Omar Ruiz: On the network side, we have strict egress rules and proxied registries. Will the install work with an internal-only container registry?
[05:17] Priya Nair: Yes. We support pulling images from private internal registries. For air-gapped, you import the images manually. We also support registries behind proxies with cert-based auth.
[05:28] Dr. Maya Santos: Any limitations on OS or Kubernetes distro? We're on RHEL and running OpenShift.
[05:34] Marco Alvarez: Our Private installer supports K8s v1.24+ and we've validated on OpenShift and vanilla upstream. The main caveat is kernel and NVIDIA driver versions for GPUs; we'll provide a compatibility matrix.
[05:48] Ken Ito: Can you explain the difference between Dedicated and Private again? I want to be precise for procurement docs.
[05:53] Jordan Lee: Sure — Dedicated is hosted by Redwood in dedicated GPU pools we reserve for you in the cloud; network is managed by us but you get tenant isolation. Private is run inside your network — on-prem or in your cloud VPC where you control the network, data residency, and security posture. Dedicated still involves outbound management plane calls to our control plane.
[06:13] Ken Ito: So Dedicated is out for us because of the no-egress constraint.
[06:17] Jordan Lee: Understandable. Many reg customers pick Private for that reason.
[06:21] Lina Park: On licensing, do we get perpetual model weights or are they licensed?
[06:26] Priya Nair: Model licensing varies by model. For open models we typically provide the weights under the model's license; for proprietary models there may be restrictions and different pricing. We'll clarify which variants you're interested in and include license terms.
[06:39] Omar Ruiz: One more technical — how do you handle KV cache persistence across restarts? Our workloads rely on warm caches.
[06:46] Priya Nair: The runtime supports KV cache checkpointing; for on-prem installs you can persist cache to a local NFS or in-memory if you want speed. We'll share recommended patterns.
[06:57] Ken Ito: For the pilot, can we do a small cluster with 2 nodes (each with 1 GPU) and validate?
[07:02] Priya Nair: Yes, that's typical. We usually recommend starting with 1-2 nodes for functional validation and then scale. For throughput testing you'll want more nodes.
[07:12] Jordan Lee: Can we capture success criteria for the pilot? Maya, what's the timeline and what would you consider success?
[07:18] Dr. Maya Santos: Timeline — procurement and budget decisions by end of month, want install in Sept. Success = pass security validation, achieve our latency target (<=150ms for 8k with 2 concurrent sessions), and integrated KMS/HSM flow.
[07:32] Jordan Lee: Great. We'll aim for that.
[07:35] Marco Alvarez: Also we'll include an example runbook for the import, a checklist for pre-reqs (drivers, K8s version, disk, etc.), and a sample playbook for benching keys.
[07:47] Ken Ito: About disk — what's your recommended storage for model weights and cache? We currently have limited NVMe capacity and probably need to add drives.
[07:55] Priya Nair: For model weights: NVMe or fast SSD is recommended, with ~1.5-2x the model size for working sets and cache. For larger models consider NFS for cold storage plus local NVMe for hot weights. We'll provide sizing guidance.
[08:11] Omar Ruiz: Any split between CPU and GPU responsibilities? Our inference engine sometimes loads CPU-heavy pre/post processing.
[08:18] Priya Nair: Yes we recommend 8-16 cores per GPU for preprocessing and batching overhead, but exact depends on your model and preprocess pipeline. We'll include a recommended baseline.
[08:29] Dr. Maya Santos: Security question — do you run any third-party dependencies that could call home? E.g., telemetry libs, crash reporters.
[08:36] Marco Alvarez: The default package includes optional telemetry which we can build out. For air-gapped installs we strip or disable those libraries; the package can be validated before import.
[08:47] Ken Ito: What's the escalation path if we hit a performance bug? We need an SLA.
[08:52] Jordan Lee: For Private customers we offer support tiers. SLA response times depend on the tier. We'll include an enterprise support add-on with faster response and a named technical contact.
[09:02] Lina Park: Can Redwood sign our MSSP/BAA? We're handling PHI in some workflows.
[09:07] Jordan Lee: We can engage legal; Redwood has customers that require BAA. We'll flag legal to follow up.
[09:14] Dr. Maya Santos: Good. For the procurement docs, can you give a ballpark on licensing model — per-GPU, per-seat, or hybrid?
[09:21] Jordan Lee: Typically on-prem is a capacity-based license (per GPU or per node) plus a support fee. We'll provide options (per-GPU perpetual + annual support, or a term license).
[09:33] Omar Ruiz: Back to offline updates — do you provide a checksum/signature to validate images? We have strict supply chain controls.
[09:39] Priya Nair: Yes, signed artifacts with cryptographic signatures and SHA256 checksums are part of the process. You can validate signatures against our public key which you can rotate.
[09:50] Ken Ito: Great. Also interested in the automated regression alerts you mentioned — can that run locally?
[09:56] Priya Nair: It can. Redwood Optimize can run locally in your environment and produce alerts; otherwise you can upload metrics to our hosted Optimize if that fits your policy. For strict air-gapped we recommend running the eval harness internally.
[10:10] Marco Alvarez: Quick note — some customers run a hybrid where the control plane is in a secured VPC with restricted egress and data plane is air-gapped; that can reduce ops. But since you said no egress, you likely need full on-prem.
[10:25] Dr. Maya Santos: Right, full on-prem likely.
[10:28] Jordan Lee: Any other blockers?
[10:30] Ken Ito: Procurement needs budget numbers. We also need an initial quote for a pilot (2 nodes with A100s) and for a production 4-node cluster on H100s for future planning.
[10:40] Jordan Lee: We'll get pricing for both configurations. Priya, can you note the hardware baseline?
[10:44] Priya Nair: Baseline: for pilot — 2 nodes, each with 1x A100 80GB or similar, 512GB RAM, 2TB NVMe. For production — 4 nodes with 1x H100 recommended, 1-2 TB NVMe per node, 768GB+ RAM. We'll attach a detailed sizing sheet.
[10:58] Omar Ruiz: Does Redwood provide prebuilt containers or do we rebuild locally?
[11:03] Marco Alvarez: We provide prebuilt, signed containers. For extra assurance, customers sometimes rebuild from source in their environment and compare digests.
[11:12] Dr. Maya Santos: Let's talk timeline — we need a procurement packet by 2026-08-28. Can you commit?
[11:18] Jordan Lee: Yes, we'll target that.
[11:20] Marco Alvarez: Also sending runbook, compatibility matrix, and the compliance pack.
[11:25] Ken Ito: One more — training and knowledge transfer. Will Redwood help with SRE handoff?
[11:30] Jordan Lee: Yes, the PS engagement includes a knowledge transfer and a runbook walkthrough. We also have written docs.
[11:36] Lina Park: Ok good. Any concerns about our current infra? We're on-prem VMware for VMs but plan to use bare-metal for GPUs.
[11:43] Priya Nair: Bare-metal with direct GPU passthrough is ideal. VMware can work but adds complexity; we'll include notes on driver setups.
[11:53] Dr. Maya Santos: Alright, let's recap next steps.
[11:57] Jordan Lee: Recap: We'll send compliance docs, on-prem checklist, pricing for pilot & production configs, GPU sizing sheet, and schedule a deep-dive on 2026-08-26 for infra. You'll share KMS/HSM diagram and procurement timeline by 2026-08-24.
[12:14] Dr. Maya Santos: Sounds good. Thank you everyone.
[12:17] Jordan Lee: Thanks all, we'll follow up via email with materials.
[12:20] END TRANSCRIPT

Notes on transcription: occasional words normalized; product names sometimes shortened ("Private" referred to as "private control plane"), small mis-hearings: "Redwood Dedicate" heard at one point, timestamps approximate.
